title: Phase Stability and Anisotropic Superconductivity in Ternary M2B4C2 (M=Ca, Mg) Monolayer
authors: Jakkapat Seeyangnok, Udomsilp Pinsook, Graeme J Ackland
abstract: In this work, we investigate the phase stability, electronic structure, and superconducting properties of the two-dimensional ternary borocarbides MB$_4$C$_2$ (M = Ca, Mg) using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Ab initio molecular dynamics, phonon dispersion, and elastic constant calculations confirm that both monolayers are dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable. Electronic structure analysis reveals an intrinsic metallic nature with a multiband Fermi surface, where states near the $Γ$ point are dominated by in-plane B-$p_x$, $p_y$ orbitals, while zone-boundary states are primarily derived from out-of-plane B-$p_z$ orbitals. The electron-phonon coupling is determined to be $λ= 0.64$ for both materials, driven by the rigid covalent B-B and B-C honeycomb networks. By solving the anisotropic Eliashberg equations, we predict that CaB$_4$C$_2$ and MgB$_4$C$_2$ are nodeless two-gap superconductors with critical temperatures ($T_c$) of 33.4 K and 33.8 K, respectively, at a Coulomb pseudopotential of $μ= 0.10$. Furthermore, the superconducting state remains robust under increased Coulomb repulsion ($μ= 0.13$), retaining elevated $T_c$ values of 31.2 K and 30.9 K, respectively. These findings establish MB$_4$C$_2$ monolayers as promising candidates for nanoscale superconducting applications and enrich the family of two-dimensional multigap superconductors.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the stability and superconductivity of 2D borocarbides $	ext{M}_2	ext{B}_4	ext{C}_2$. Using advanced first-principles methods, the authors confirm the structural robustness and predict that both $	ext{Ca}$ and $	ext{Mg}$ compounds are high-$T_c$, two-gap superconductors. The work establishes these materials as promising candidates for nanoscale superconducting devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the phase stability, electronic structure, and superconducting properties of two-dimensional ternary borocarbides, $	ext{M}_2	ext{B}_4	ext{C}_2$ ($	ext{M} = 	ext{Ca}, 	ext{Mg}$).
main_result: Both $	ext{CaB}_4	ext{C}_2$ and $	ext{MgB}_4	ext{C}_2$ monolayers are predicted to be stable, nodeless, two-gap superconductors with high critical temperatures ($T_c \approx 33 	ext{ K}$).
method: The research employs first-principles calculations (DFT) combined with fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory to model electron-phonon coupling and superconductivity.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{M}_2	ext{B}_4	ext{C}_2$ monolayer, which is analyzed for its structural, electronic, and superconducting characteristics.
key_observables: Critical temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling constant ($\lambda$), superconducting energy gaps ($\Delta_1, \Delta_2$), and mechanical/thermal stability metrics.
important_parameters: Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*=0.10$ or $0.13$), temperature ($300 	ext{ K}$), and material identity ($	ext{Ca}$ vs. $	ext{Mg}$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on DFT approximations and the validity of the Migdal-Eliashberg theory for describing superconductivity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, AIMD simulations showing thermal stability, and potentially the momentum-resolved electron-phonon coupling and superconducting gap structure.
paper_structure: The paper follows a logical progression: first establishing structural and thermal stability via AIMD and elastic constants; second, characterizing the electronic structure and bonding; and finally, applying anisotropic Eliashberg theory to predict the superconducting state and $T_c$.
why_interesting: While the focus is on solid-state superconductivity, the use of advanced many-body theory (Eliashberg equations) and the analysis of anisotropic pairing mechanisms provide rich theoretical material relevant to strongly correlated systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Side view and (b) top view of the crystal structure of MB4C2 (M =Ca, Mg) in space group P3m1 (No. 156). Light blue, green, and brown spheres represent M, B, and C atoms, respectively.

FIG. 2. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations of the MB4C2 monolayers at 300 K for 10 ps. The results are shown for (a) CaB4C2, and (b) MgB4C2. In each panel, the left side displays the final structural snapshot of the 2×2 supercell at the end of the sim- ulation. The right side shows the time evolution of the temperature T(t) (orange line, right axis) and the total energy variation per atom E(t)−E0 (blue line, left axis).

FIG. 3. Electronic band structures, projected density of states (PDOS), and Fermi surfaces for monolayer (a) AlB4C2, (b) CaB4C2, and (c) MgB4C2. In the band structure plots, orbital contributions are highlighted by open circles, where the marker size corresponds to the spectral weight of the specified state. The horizontal solid line at zero energy indicates the Fermi level (EF). The dashed black hexagons represent the first Brillouin zone for the Fermi surfaces.

FIG. 4. Three-dimensional spatial distributions of (a) the electron lo- calization function (ELF) and (b) the local electron density evaluated at the Fermi level (EF) for the MB4C2 systems. The ELF highlights the strong covalent bonds within the honeycomb network, while the local density at EF visualizes the p-orbital character of the conduc- tion electrons.

FIG. 5. Schematic representation of the atomic displacement pat- terns for the optical phonon modes at the Brillouin zone center (Γ point) of the MB4C2 monolayers. Each panel is labeled with the cor- responding mode index (based specifically on the CaB4C2 system), symmetry, irreducible representation, and optical activity (R for Ra- man, I for Infrared). Red arrows indicate the direction and relative amplitude of the atomic vibrations.
